question.worked_solution:
The roots of $f(h)$ are the solutions to the equation $f(h)=0.$ In our case, we have

$$
\frac{{h}^{2}+9h+20}{{h}^{3}+3{h}^{2}-25h-75}=0.
$$

First, we factor the numerator and denominator and cancel any common factors, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(h) & =\frac{{h}^{2}+9h+20}{{h}^{3}+3{h}^{2}-25h-75} \\  & =\frac{(h+5)(h+4)}{{h}^{2}(h+3)-25(h+3)} \\  & =\frac{(h+5)(h+4)}{({h}^{2}-25)(h+3)} \\  & =\frac{(h+5)(h+4)}{(h+5)(h-5)(h+3)} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{(h+5)}(h+4)}{\cancel{(h+5)}(h-5)(h+3)} \\  & =\frac{h+4}{(h-5)(h+3)}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set the numerator equal to zero and solve for $h:$

$$
\begin{aligned}h+4=0\,⟹\,h=-4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to $f(h)=0$ is $h=-4.$
